summary: This is a Mol Labs public report (card N32) proposing an assumption-kill experiment to test whether baclofen retains residual cognition/antinociception/motor phenotype under GABA-B genetic loss-of-function (Gabbr1 KO) or GABA-B-matched antagonism (CGP 35348-class) that abolishes GABA-B-class attribution. The document is a research discussion/hypothesis card at TRL 1–2: no new experiments have been run (execution_status=NOT_RUN), but it synthesizes four key prior-art literature anchors and defines a pre-registered prediction framework. The claim is that residual baclofen phenotype ≥50% of baclofen-alone under GABA-B abolish would constitute a non-GABA-B bridge kill; current evidence from Malcangio and Schuler argues against residual-positive, and the matched H2H residual result remains UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Document Overview and Hypothesis (N32)
content_blocks.content: Mol Labs public report card N32. Status: NEGATIVE (assumption-kill). Execution: NOT_RUN. The central question is whether any residual baclofen phenotype (cognition / antinociception / motor) survives a Gabbr1 LOF or GABA-B-matched antagonism (CGP 35348-class) that abolishes GABA-B-class attribution on the same panel. The hypothesis is framed as a 'gabab-insufficiency assumption-kill': if baclofen is truly a selective GABA-B agonist, residual phenotype under GABA-B abolish should be empty; a residual-positive result would imply a non-GABA-B bridge. ip_class=gabab-insufficiency; kill_cost_tier=1; time_to_refute=4w; vault_hold=no; fto_status=UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Formal Claim / Pre-registered Prediction
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered acute/subacute rodent (McNamara/Kaupmann/Malcangio/Schuler-class) cognition / antinociception / motor panel with a baclofen-alone (or baclofen vs vehicle) arm on GABA-B-intact concurrent controls, a GABA-B genetic LOF (Gabbr1 / GABA-B(1)) or GABA-B-matched antagonism (e.g. CGP 35348-class) that abolishes GABA-B-class antinociception / motor / cognition attribution, and a baclofen-under-abolish arm: under the same condition that abolishes GABA-B-class attribution, baclofen retains residual phenotype ≥50% of baclofen-alone (or baclofen vs vehicle Δ) on GABA-B-intact concurrent controls (cognition / antinociception / motor units as pre-specified; α/N pre-specified). Threshold: ≥50% residual = assumption-kill / gabab-insufficiency.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary — Four Literature Anchors
content_blocks.content:
Four key prior-art references are cited:
1. McNamara & Skelton (PMID 8808136, Pharmacol Biochem Behav 1996, DOI 10.1016/0091-3057(95)02025-x): Baclofen dose-dependently impairs spatial learning in rats (Morris water maze + open-field locomotion). Cognitive phenotype prior; intact GABA-B present; NO Gabbr1-KO or CGP-35348 abolish residual arm (Q_mcnamara_cgp=0). DOI HEAD 200 verified.
2. Kaupmann et al. (PMID 9069281, Nature 1997, DOI 10.1038/386239a0): Expression cloning of GABA(B) receptors — Gabbr1 molecular identity. CRITICAL: identity ≠ residual H2H. DOI HEAD 200 verified.
3. Malcangio (PMID 1653069, Br J Pharmacol 1991, DOI 10.1111/j.1476-5381.1991.tb09784.x, PMC1908386): CGP 35348 prevents baclofen antinociception and muscle-relaxant effect in mouse/rat hot-plate/writhing/paw-pressure + rota-rod assays. CGP matched-block TOOL + necessity AGAINST residual on antinoc/motor. CRITICAL: prevention ≠ residual+. DOI HEAD 403 (NCBI/PMC verified).
4. Schuler et al. (PMID 11498050, Neuron 2001, DOI 10.1016/s0896-6273(01)00345-2): Mice lacking GABA-B(1) — epilepsy, hyperalgesia, impaired memory, loss of pre- and postsynaptic GABA-B responses; GABA-B agonist muscle relaxation/hypothermia/delta EEG LOST in null. Gabbr1 KO tool + necessity AGAINST residual. CRITICAL: do NOT misread as baclofen-in-KO residual+. DOI HEAD 200 verified.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Measured / Evidence State
content_blocks.content:
Current evidence state:
- McNamara baclofen spatial-learning LITERATURE phenotype prior without Gabbr1/CGP-abolish residual arm (PMID 8808136; Q_mcnamara_cgp=0).
- Kaupmann Gabbr1 LITERATURE identity — NOT residual H2H (PMID 9069281).
- Malcangio CGP 35348 LITERATURE tool + necessity AGAINST residual on antinoc/motor — prevention ≠ residual+ (PMID 1653069/PMC1908386).
- Schuler Gabbr1 KO LITERATURE tool + necessity AGAINST residual — agonist muscle/hypothermia/delta EEG LOST in null; do NOT misread as baclofen-in-KO residual+ (PMID 11498050).
- Adjacent NON-MATCH: PMID 12970075 (baclofen hypothermia abolished in Gabbr1-/- — necessity AGAINST); PMID 10094428 (gabapentin ≠ baclofen); PMID 22761875 (GB1-alone ERK ≠ Gabbr1 LOF residual).
- Matched residual-positive baclofen under Gabbr1 LOF or CGP 35348 block: UNKNOWN as residual-positive (soft-complete Q_resid_life_h2h=0 EMPTY; Q_resid_tight=52 NON-MATCH/necessity-AGAINST; Q_resid=774 inflated NON-MATCH; Q_baclofen_in_ko=20 necessity-leaning).
- PRIOR_ART PARTIAL: phenotype + Gabbr1 identity + CGP/Gabbr1 tools FOUND; residual-positive under abolish ABSENT.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch and Experimental Design Preference
content_blocks.content:
Gabab-insufficiency assumption-kill: baclofen moves cognition/antinociception/motor phenotypes and is framed as selective GABA-B agonism. Gabbr1 LOF is a genetic tool (Schuler); published phenotype prior is McNamara spatial-learning impairment; Gabbr1 molecular identity is Kaupmann; CGP 35348 is a GABA-B antagonist pharmacological tool with necessity AGAINST residual on antinoc/motor (Malcangio). No published head-to-head scores residual-positive baclofen cognition/antinociception/motor under Gabbr1 LOF or GABA-B-matched antagonism that abolishes GABA-B-class attribution on the same panel as a retained residual ≥50% of baclofen-alone.
Preferred execution path: cell/slice/block-QC before new animal (e.g. CGP abolish of a GABA-B-class control response — electrophys/receptor QC — for abolish gate); in vivo McNamara/Malcangio/Schuler-class rodent cognition/antinociception/motor panel remains the primary kill path.

content_blocks.title: Refute Condition and Competing Caveats
content_blocks.content:
Refute if: On the pre-registered acute/subacute rodent panel, under Gabbr1 genetic LOF or CGP 35348-class abolish that abolishes GABA-B-class attribution, residual baclofen phenotype falls below 50% of baclofen-alone (or baclofen vs vehicle Δ) on GABA-B-intact concurrent controls — so GABA-B-class sufficiency for the baclofen phenotype survives and gabab-insufficiency fails — when abolish-gate, baclofen-alone/intact-arm comparator, and power/assay artifacts are ruled out.
Competing caveats (inconclusive rather than refuted): abolish condition fails to kill GABA-B-class attribution / baclofen-alone null / underpowered strata / assay-identity mismatch (phenotype ≠ residual; Malcangio CGP prevention ≠ residual+; Schuler agonist-loss ≠ baclofen-in-KO residual+; Kaupmann identity ≠ residual proof; hypothermia abolish ≠ cognition residual; gabapentin ≠ baclofen; Gabbr1 ≠ Htr1a; GABA-B ≠ GABA-A; Gabbr1 ≠ AMPAR/GlyT1/NMDAR/PDE4/SERT/NET).

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations and Execution Constraints
content_blocks.content:
Key constraints:
1. N1–N31 do not prove N32; especially N31 (buspirone×Htr1a ≠ baclofen×Gabbr1; Q_N31_collapse=0) and P21 (Selank×GABA-A ≠ baclofen×Gabbr1; Q_P21_selank=0; Q_P21_gabaA_resid=0) are CRITICAL DISTINCT.
2. PRIOR_ART PARTIAL OK — not auto-REJECT; residual-positive under abolish EMPTY (Q_resid_life_h2h=0); do not invent residual-positive H2H.
3. Prefer cell/slice/block-QC before new animal; lock same-panel acute/subacute rodent cognition/antinociception/motor with baclofen ± Gabbr1 LOF or GABA-B-matched challenge as primary kill path.
4. No dosing; NOT MB/MAOI; orthosteric_drift=false; do not burn ip_class=none; do not collapse to N31 Htr1a or P21 GABA-A.
5. Baclofen IS a selective GABA-B agonist — empty residual is expected; residual-positive would imply non-GABA-B bridge (strong kill).
6. Execution_status=NOT_RUN; fto_status=UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical ablations identified:
1. Remove same-panel contrast of residual baclofen cognition/antinociception/motor under Gabbr1 LOF or GABA-B-matched antagonism: Without the abolish×residual H2H on a McNamara/Kaupmann/Malcangio/Schuler-class panel with a baclofen arm, separate phenotype LITERATURE and GABA-B tool/necessity LITERATURE cannot show gabab-insufficiency as a residual-positive kill.
2. Remove verified abolish gate plus baclofen-alone/intact-arm comparator: Without verified GABA-B-class abolish and baclofen-alone/intact-arm comparator under the same condition, residual baclofen is just 'another GABAergic agent under nonspecific challenge,' not an assumption-kill.
3. Remove N31≠N32 + P21≠N32 + adjacent-NON-MATCH≠residual+ discipline: Treating N15–N31 residuals or Malcangio prevention or Schuler agonist-loss as residual-under-abolish would invent an H2H result left UNKNOWN as residual-positive.
